cards.q: US legal category of herbal and vitamin supplements
cards.a: Foods, not drugs (regulated as dietary supplements under DSHEA 1994)

cards.q: Premarket proof demanded of supplements in the USA
cards.a: None for efficacy or safety; products assumed safe as directed

cards.q: Exception to presumed safety of a supplement ingredient
cards.a: New dietary ingredient: manufacturer must give some safety data before marketing

cards.q: Who must prove harm before a supplement is removed from market
cards.a: The FDA

cards.q: Claim type printed on supplement labels
cards.a: Structure-function claims (maintain normal structure or function)

cards.q: DSHEA 1994 definition of dietary supplement
cards.a: Vitamins, minerals, herbs/botanicals, amino acids, and their concentrates, metabolites, extracts

cards.q: Why DSHEA GMP standards were slow
cards.a: FDA final GMP rule only in 2007, a 13-year delay

cards.q: Result of supplement self-regulation
cards.a: Adulteration, misbranding and contamination

cards.q: DNA barcoding finding on botanical products (44 products, 30 species)
cards.a: Species substitution in 32% of samples

cards.q: Quality problems in herbal supplements: list all
cards.a: Botanical misidentification; lack of purity; variable potency and purification

cards.q: Reasons FDA oversight of supplements is weak: list all
cards.a: Limited resources; overseas ingredient suppliers; complex supply chain; sales incentive

cards.q: Who must report serious supplement adverse events (2006 law)
cards.a: Manufacturers, packers and distributors, to the FDA

cards.q: Serious adverse events for supplement reporting: list all
cards.a: Death; life-threatening event; hospitalisation; persistent or significant disability; congenital anomaly; intervention needed to prevent these

cards.q: Why natural does not mean safe
cards.a: Botanicals may be inherently inert or toxic

cards.q: Why supplement adverse effects are under-recognised
cards.a: Consumers rarely report them; products seldom chemically analysed

cards.q: Tests seldom done on marketed supplements
cards.a: Dose-response, toxicity, mutagenicity, carcinogenicity, teratogenicity

cards.q: Why botanical drug interactions are hard to study
cards.a: Hundreds of active and inactive ingredients per botanical

cards.q: Lead sources in folk remedies and cosmetics
cards.a: Azarcon and greta (Mexican remedies), certain Ayurvedic preparations, kohl eye cosmetic

cards.q: Mercury sources in folk medicines and cosmetics
cards.a: Skin-lightening creams and folk remedies; also antiseptics

cards.q: Stimulants in fat burners and ma-huang
cards.a: Caffeine in "metabolic enhancer" or "fat burner" supplements; ephedrine in ma-huang

cards.q: Herbs to use cautiously or not at all (Table 65-1): list all
cards.a: Aconite; aristolochia; black cohosh; borage; chaparral; coltsfoot; comfrey; ephedra (ma-huang); germander; gland extracts; placenta derivatives; Jin Bu Huan; kava-kava; kratom; pennyroyal; poke root; royal jelly; sassafras

cards.q: Aconite (Aconitum): intended use and toxicity
cards.a: Analgesic; alkaloid cardiac and CNS toxicity

cards.q: Aristolochia (aristolochic acid): intended use and toxicity
cards.a: Traditional Chinese medicine; carcinogen and nephrotoxicity

cards.q: Black cohosh: menopausal use and main toxicity
cards.a: Hepatotoxicity, rare given widespread use

cards.q: Borage: intended use and toxicity
cards.a: Anti-inflammatory, diuretic; pyrrolizidine alkaloid hepatotoxicity

cards.q: Chaparral: intended use and toxicity
cards.a: Anti-infective, antioxidant, anticancer; hepatotoxicity

cards.q: Coltsfoot: intended use and toxicity
cards.a: Upper respiratory infections; pyrrolizidine alkaloid hepatotoxicity

cards.q: Comfrey: intended use and toxicity
cards.a: Internal digestive aid, topical wound healing; pyrrolizidine alkaloids

cards.q: Comfrey: safe use per Table 65-1
cards.a: Avoid ingestion; topical leaves for up to 4-6 weeks

cards.q: Ephedra (ma-huang): intended use and toxicity
cards.a: Diet aid, stimulant, bronchodilator; CNS and cardiac toxicity

cards.q: Germander: main toxicity
cards.a: Hepatotoxicity

cards.q: Gland-derived extracts (thymus, adrenal, thyroid): main risks
cards.a: Transmission of bacteria, viruses or prions; variable hormone content

cards.q: Human placenta derivatives: main risk
cards.a: Transmission of bacteria, viruses or prions

cards.q: Kava-kava: main toxicity
cards.a: Hepatotoxicity

cards.q: Kratom (Mitragyna speciosa): toxicities
cards.a: Dependence, withdrawal, respiratory depression, hallucinations, seizures, hepatotoxicity, death

cards.q: Pennyroyal: toxic agent and organ damage
cards.a: Pulegone and its metabolite: liver failure and renal failure

cards.q: Poke root: main toxicity
cards.a: Hemorrhagic gastritis

cards.q: Royal jelly: main toxicity
cards.a: Bronchospasm and anaphylaxis

cards.q: Sassafras: main toxicity
cards.a: Safrole oil, hepatocarcinogen in animals

cards.q: WHO quality practices for herbal medicines: list all
cards.a: GACP (cultivation and collection), GMP (manufacture), GSP (marketing)

cards.q: Where herbal quality problems start
cards.a: At cultivation in the field

cards.q: Why not all herbal products qualify as medicines
cards.a: Breaches of GMP in manufacture

cards.q: Evidence gap for traditional medicines
cards.a: No well-controlled trials, double-blind studies or well-documented case records

cards.q: Common flaw in ethnopharmacology bioassays
cards.a: Use of high extract concentrations to show a response

cards.q: Indian legal category for phytopharmaceuticals (NDCT Rules 2019)
cards.a: Added to the definition of new drug

cards.q: Phytopharmaceutical drug: definition
cards.a: Purified, standardised fraction of a plant extract with at least four defined compounds; not parenteral

cards.q: Minimum defined compounds in a phytopharmaceutical
cards.a: Four bioactive or phytochemical compounds

cards.q: Route excluded from the phytopharmaceutical definition
cards.a: Parenteral

cards.q: Indian reply time for phytopharmaceutical clinical trial applications
cards.a: 30 days; no reply in that time means deemed approved

cards.q: Medicines that phytopharmaceuticals are distinct from in India
cards.a: Ayurvedic, Unani or Siddha medicines

cards.q: Bodies promoting standards for plant-based medicine (examples)
cards.a: WHO; European Agency for the Evaluation of Medicinal Products; European Scientific Cooperation on Phytomedicine; US AHCPR; European Pharmacopoeia Commission

cards.q: Echinacea species most widely used: list all
cards.a: Echinacea purpurea, E pallida, E angustifolia

cards.q: Echinacea constituents by type: list all
cards.a: Flavonoids; alkamides and polyacetylenes; polysaccharides; caffeoyl conjugates (echinacoside, cichoric acid, caffeic acid)

cards.q: Echinacea constituents most often credited with immune modulation
cards.a: Cichoric acid, echinacoside, alkamides and polysaccharides

cards.q: Echinacea in colds: Cochrane review (24 trials)
cards.a: No significant benefit in treating colds overall

cards.q: Echinacea cold prevention meta-analysis (14 trials)
cards.a: 58% lower risk of clear cold; symptoms 1.25 days shorter (confounded)

cards.q: Recent echinacea systematic review: prevention and duration
cards.a: Relative risk 0.78 for cold prevention; no shorter duration

cards.q: Echinacea pediatric trial (200 children aged 4-12)
cards.a: Echinaforce junior 1200 mg/day beat vitamin C 150 mg/day over 4 months

cards.q: Echinacea uses needing more research: list all
cards.a: Haematological recovery after chemotherapy; urinary and vaginal fungal infections; HPV condyloma relapse

cards.q: Echinacea in recurrent genital herpes
cards.a: Ineffective (E purpurea)

cards.q: Echinacea adverse effects with oral products
cards.a: Unpleasant taste, GI upset, allergic rash (rash more in children)

cards.q: Echinacea in pregnancy and lactation
cards.a: Only after consulting the health care provider, especially alcoholic extracts

cards.q: Maximum continuous echinacea use for colds
cards.a: 10-14 days

cards.q: Avoid echinacea in: list all
cards.a: Immune deficiency (AIDS, cancer); autoimmune disease (MS, RA); people on immunosuppressants (theory)

cards.q: Echinacea and warfarin in healthy subjects
cards.a: No effect on warfarin pharmacodynamics or platelet aggregation

cards.q: Echinacea and HIV protease inhibitors
cards.a: No effect on lopinavir, ritonavir, etravirine or darunavir levels

cards.q: Echinacea preparation preferred for colds (adults)
cards.a: Standardised aerial-part E purpurea alcoholic extract or pressed juice, started within 24 h

cards.q: Echinaforce in vitro virucidal targets: list all
cards.a: Influenza A and B, parainfluenza, herpes simplex, HCoV-229E, SARS-CoV-1 and -2

cards.q: Garlic: alliin converted by alliinase to what
cards.a: Allicin, the odour principle

cards.q: Why garlic powder is enteric coated
cards.a: Protects alliinase from gastric acid

cards.q: Aged garlic extract: odour and constituents
cards.a: Odour-free; no alliin or allicin; standardised to S-allylcysteine

cards.q: Dried garlic powder standardisation
cards.a: 1.3% alliin, or allicin-generating potential of 0.6%

cards.q: Garlic in vitro cardiovascular action
cards.a: Allicin inhibits HMG-CoA reductase; antioxidant

cards.q: Garlic effect on lipids (meta-analysis)
cards.a: Total cholesterol about -15 mg/dL, LDL about -6 mg/dL; triglycerides unchanged

cards.q: Duration needed for garlic lipid benefit in dyslipidaemia
cards.a: Beyond 8 weeks

cards.q: Garlic in diabetes
cards.a: Lowers fasting glucose and HbA1c in diabetics, not in healthy people

cards.q: Garlic blood pressure effect in hypertension
cards.a: Systolic -8.6 and diastolic -6.1 mm Hg; no effect if normal or prehypertensive

cards.q: Proposed mechanisms of garlic BP lowering: list all
cards.a: Nitric oxide synthase stimulation; ACE inhibition; increased hydrogen sulfide

cards.q: Garlic antiplatelet mechanisms proposed
cards.a: Inhibits thromboxane synthesis or stimulates nitric oxide synthesis

cards.q: Garlic 4-year trial in coronary disease
cards.a: Less carotid and femoral plaque than placebo; death, stroke and MI not assessed

cards.q: Aged garlic extract and coronary calcification (1 year)
cards.a: Slowed calcification progression in small trials (104 patients); IL-6 fell

cards.q: Garlic antimicrobial mechanism
cards.a: Allicin inhibits thiol-containing enzymes of microbes

cards.q: Garlic and colds: evidence
cards.a: Allicin 180 mg daily for 12 weeks reduced colds; only one trial qualified

cards.q: Garlic intake and cancer risk (umbrella review)
cards.a: Odds ratio 0.51 for gastric cancer; 0.77 for prostate cancer

cards.q: Garlic adverse effects: GI and bleeding
cards.a: Stomach upset, nausea, bloating, flatulence (6%), hypotension (1.3%), allergy (1.1%), rare bleeding

cards.q: Garlic odour adverse effect
cards.a: Breath and body odour in 20-40% with enteric-coated powder

cards.q: Garlic contact reaction
cards.a: Dermatitis from handling raw garlic

cards.q: Supplements with antiplatelet effect, avoid with anticoagulants or aspirin: list all
cards.a: Garlic; ginkgo; ginseng

cards.q: Drugs needing caution with garlic (anticlotting): list all
cards.a: Warfarin, newer oral anticoagulants, aspirin, ibuprofen

cards.q: Garlic and saquinavir
cards.a: Reduces saquinavir bioavailability; no effect on ritonavir

cards.q: Daily dose of powdered garlic
cards.a: 600-900 mg, about one raw clove (2-4 g)

cards.q: Aged garlic extract daily dose range
cards.a: 600-1800 mg/day; up to 7200 mg used for 6 months

cards.q: Ginkgo leaf extract: crude leaf to extract ratio
cards.a: 50 parts crude leaf to 1 part extract

cards.q: Ginkgo haemodynamic effects
cards.a: Increased blood flow, reduced viscosity, vasodilation; enhanced endogenous nitric oxide

cards.q: Ginkgo in intermittent claudication
cards.a: Non-significant gain in pain-free walking (64.5 m); standardised extract lacks benefit

cards.q: Ginkgo to prevent dementia (GEM and GuidAge, 5-6 years, about 3000 elderly)
cards.a: No benefit with 240 mg/day EGb761; no effect on BP or cardiovascular events

cards.q: Symptoms covered by "cerebral insufficiency": list all
cards.a: Poor concentration, confusion, anxiety, depression, hearing loss, headache

cards.q: Cochrane review of ginkgo in dementia and mild cognitive impairment (36 trials)
cards.a: Effects unpredictable and unlikely to be clinically relevant

cards.q: EGb761 dementia trials with stricter entry: dose that helped global assessment
cards.a: 240 mg/day; 120 mg/day did not

cards.q: 2019 consensus on EGb761 in dementia
cards.a: Single agent in some AD or vascular dementia; add-on to cholinesterase inhibitors or memantine; not for prevention

cards.q: Ginkgo add-on in chronic schizophrenia
cards.a: Preliminary benefit on negative symptoms with standard drugs (Chinese trials)

cards.q: Other ginkgo trial conditions, insufficient evidence: list all
cards.a: Generalised anxiety disorder; tardive dyskinesia; bronchoconstriction; short-term memory; acute ischaemic stroke; type 2 diabetes; erectile dysfunction; tinnitus and hearing loss; macular degeneration

cards.q: Ginkgo in aged animals: receptor changes
cards.a: Muscarinic and 5-HT1A receptors up; adrenoceptors down

cards.q: Ginkgo adverse effects, similar to placebo
cards.a: Nausea, headache, stomach upset, diarrhoea, allergy, anxiety, insomnia

cards.q: Ginkgo case-report interactions: list all
cards.a: Efavirenz (virologic failure); trazodone (sedation); risperidone (priapism); valproic acid and phenytoin (seizures)

cards.q: Ginkgo seizure risk: cause
cards.a: Ginkgotoxin in seeds, contaminating leaf products; avoid in seizure disorders

cards.q: Ginkgo dried leaf extract standardisation
cards.a: 24% flavone glycosides and 6% terpene lactones

cards.q: Ginkgo dose studied in dementia
cards.a: 240 mg/day dried extract in two divided doses

cards.q: Panax species most available in the USA: list all
cards.a: P ginseng (Chinese or Korean); P quinquefolius (American)

cards.q: Ginseng active principles
cards.a: Triterpenoid saponin glycosides (ginsenosides), about 30 types

cards.q: Ginseng standardisation
cards.a: 4-10% ginsenosides

cards.q: Ginseng metabolite formed by gut flora
cards.a: Compound K

cards.q: Siberian ginseng: species and main constituent
cards.a: Eleutherococcus senticosus; eleutherosides, no ginsenosides

cards.q: Brazilian ginseng: species
cards.a: Pfaffia paniculata (not a Panax)

cards.q: Ginseng claimed use
cards.a: Adaptogen: improves physical and mental performance under stress

cards.q: Ginseng and fasting glucose (20 trials, pre-diabetes and type 2)
cards.a: Fasting glucose about -7 mg/dL; HbA1c unchanged

cards.q: Ginseng for cold prevention in healthy seniors
cards.a: Possibly fewer colds and shorter duration; evidence insufficient to recommend

cards.q: Ginseng effect on blood pressure (17 trials)
cards.a: No significant effect on systolic, diastolic or mean arterial pressure

cards.q: Ginseng lipid effect at 3 g/day (metabolic syndrome)
cards.a: Small fall in total and LDL cholesterol; not clinically meaningful

cards.q: Ginseng dose for cancer-related fatigue
cards.a: 2 g daily (P quinquefolius or P ginseng); 1 g or less gives minimal benefit

cards.q: Ginsenoside Rg3 capsule (95%): where available
cards.a: China only; with chemotherapy improved survival and quality of life in trials

cards.q: Ginseng cancer evidence from case-control and cohort studies
cards.a: Non-organ-specific cancer prevention with long-term use

cards.q: Ginseng effects with the best support: list all
cards.a: Cold prevention; lowering postprandial glucose; nonspecific cancer prevention; alleviating cancer-related fatigue

cards.q: Possible oestrogenic effects of ginseng (case report)
cards.a: Vaginal bleeding, breast pain, gynaecomastia

cards.q: Ginseng CNS and BP adverse effects (case reports)
cards.a: Insomnia, nervousness, mania; hypertension (methylxanthines may contribute)

cards.q: Psychiatric drugs that caused irritability or mania with ginseng: list all
cards.a: Phenelzine; lithium; neuroleptics

cards.q: Ginseng species and warfarin
cards.a: P quinquefolius reduces warfarin effect; not reported for P ginseng

cards.q: P ginseng effect on immunity (randomised, 8-12 weeks)
cards.a: Increased natural killer cell activity versus placebo

cards.q: Drugs with no relevant interaction with ginseng in a 15-day PK study: list all
cards.a: Caffeine; losartan; omeprazole; dextromethorphan; midazolam; pitavastatin

cards.q: Ginseng: use cautiously in: list all
cards.a: Psychiatric, oestrogenic and hypoglycaemic medicines; immunocompromised people; autoimmune disorders

cards.q: Standard dose of crude P ginseng root
cards.a: 1-2 g/day

cards.q: Standardised P ginseng extract equivalence
cards.a: 200 mg extract equals 1 g crude root

cards.q: Ginseng standardised extract used in trials and sold in the USA
cards.a: Ginsana

cards.q: Ginseng processing forms: white, red and black
cards.a: White: peeled, air-dried; red: steam-treated, air-dried; black: steamed nine times

cards.q: St John's wort standardisation marker
cards.a: Hypericin (older standard 0.3%)

cards.q: Constituent now favoured for St John's wort antidepressant effect
cards.a: Hyperforin (probably acting with other compounds)

cards.q: Which St John's wort constituent inhibits reuptake of serotonin, noradrenaline, dopamine
cards.a: Hyperforin (hypericin does not)

cards.q: St John's wort MAO inhibition: clinical relevance
cards.a: MAO-A/B inhibition needs concentrations above those reached clinically

cards.q: Chronic St John's wort extract effect on cortical receptors (rodents)
cards.a: Adrenoceptors down-regulated; 5-HT2 receptors up-regulated

cards.q: Other in vitro St John's wort actions: list all
cards.a: Sigma receptor binding; GABA receptor binding; prevents glutamate release; protects hippocampal cells

cards.q: St John's wort in mild to moderate depression (29 RCTs)
cards.a: Better than placebo, comparable to SSRIs and TCAs, with fewer side effects

cards.q: St John's wort onset and long-term use
cards.a: Onset 2-4 weeks; benefit beyond 12 weeks poorly studied

cards.q: St John's wort dose for mild to moderate depression
cards.a: 900 mg/day dried extract in three divided doses

cards.q: Current St John's wort standardisation
cards.a: 2-5% hyperforin (many products still 0.3% hypericin)

cards.q: St John's wort other mood uses (evidence limited): list all
cards.a: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder; climacteric complaints; somatoform disorders; anxiety

cards.q: St John's wort for hot flashes
cards.a: Reduced severity, duration and frequency vs placebo, up to 16 weeks

cards.q: Investigational photoactivated hypericin uses
cards.a: IV for HIV; intralesional for basal and squamous cell carcinoma

cards.q: What activates hypericin
cards.a: Visible or UV-A light (photolabile)

cards.q: Can patients with viral illness or cancer take the usual St John's wort extract
cards.a: No; only isolated hypericin was studied

cards.q: St John's wort photosensitisation: constituents and advice
cards.a: Hypericin and pseudohypericin; wear sunscreen and eye protection

cards.q: St John's wort rare adverse effects: list all
cards.a: GI upset, fatigue, sedation, restlessness, dizziness, headache, dry mouth

cards.q: St John's wort psychiatric adverse effects
cards.a: Hypomania, mania, autonomic arousal

cards.q: St John's wort and antidepressants or stimulants
cards.a: Serotonin syndrome risk; use cautiously or avoid

cards.q: Mechanism of St John's wort drug interactions
cards.a: Hyperforin activates PXR, inducing CYP3A4, 2C9, 1A2 and P-glycoprotein

cards.q: Which St John's wort constituent has no effect on PXR, CYP or P-glycoprotein
cards.a: Hypericin

cards.q: St John's wort subtherapeutic drug levels (case reports): list all
cards.a: Digoxin; birth control drugs (pregnancy); cyclosporine; HIV protease and NNRTI inhibitors; warfarin; rivaroxaban; irinotecan; tacrolimus; theophylline; anticonvulsants

cards.q: Advice on combining St John's wort with other medicines
cards.a: Avoid indiscriminate use, since constituent content varies

cards.q: Milk thistle active mixture and content of dried herb
cards.a: Silymarin (flavonolignans), 2-3% of dried herb

cards.q: Silymarin isomers: list all
cards.a: Silybin (50-70% of complex; most potent); silychristin; silydianin

cards.q: Limitation of oral silybin and its fix
cards.a: Poor bioavailability; nanoparticle and phosphatidylcholine formulations improve it

cards.q: Milk thistle standardisation
cards.a: 70-80% silymarin

cards.q: Silybin elimination
cards.a: Enterohepatic circulation and biliary excretion

cards.q: Milk thistle antioxidant actions (animal and in vitro): list all
cards.a: Reduces lipid peroxidation; scavenges free radicals; raises glutathione and superoxide dismutase

cards.q: Milk thistle anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic actions: list all
cards.a: Inhibits lipoxygenase and NF-kB; reduces TGF-beta (stellate cells); collagen reduced in cirrhosis model

cards.q: Unusual milk thistle mechanism claimed
cards.a: Raises RNA polymerase I in nonmalignant, not malignant, hepatocytes

cards.q: Toxins milk thistle protected against in animal models: list all
cards.a: Amanita mushrooms; galactosamine; carbon tetrachloride; acetaminophen; antituberculosis drugs; radiation; cold ischaemia; ethanol

cards.q: Milk thistle and bile flow
cards.a: Dose-dependent bile stimulation in animals; evidence insufficient for cholestasis

cards.q: Milk thistle for lactation
cards.a: Traditional use; raises rat prolactin, but no human data, so avoid

cards.q: Milk thistle with chemotherapy
cards.a: Antioxidant may affect chemotherapeutic agents; cancer data insufficient

cards.q: Conditions oral milk thistle has been used for: list all
cards.a: Acute and chronic viral hepatitis; alcoholic liver disease; toxin- and drug-induced liver injury

cards.q: Oral milk thistle systematic review (13 RCTs, 915 patients)
cards.a: No reduction in mortality, histology or complications at 6 months

cards.q: Oral milk thistle in interferon-refractory hepatitis C
cards.a: No benefit on ALT or HCV RNA at 420 or 700 mg/day

cards.q: IV silybinin in hepatitis C
cards.a: Reduced HCV RNA and ALT; HCV RNA relapsed after withdrawal

cards.q: IV silybin around liver transplantation in HCV (pilot)
cards.a: At least 14 days before and 7 days after transplant

cards.q: High-dose oral silymarin in biopsy-proven NASH (2100 mg/day, 1 year)
cards.a: No 30% histology improvement; lower fibrosis and stiffness markers

cards.q: Milk thistle as antidote in Amanita phalloides poisoning
cards.a: Not confirmed; IV silybinin (Legalon SIL) used in Europe, based on case-control data

cards.q: Milk thistle adverse effects
cards.a: Similar to placebo; laxative effect above 1500 mg/day

cards.q: Milk thistle drug-interaction risk
cards.a: No significant P-glycoprotein or CYP effect; posing no risk in humans

cards.q: Milk thistle recommended oral dose
cards.a: 280-420 mg/day silybin in three divided doses

cards.q: Saw palmetto species and main use
cards.a: Serenoa repens or Sabal serrulata; benign prostatic hyperplasia

cards.q: Saw palmetto constituents: list all
cards.a: Phytosterols (beta-sitosterol); aliphatic alcohols; polyprenic compounds; flavonoids

cards.q: Saw palmetto standardisation
cards.a: 85-95% fatty acids and sterols

cards.q: Saw palmetto in vitro actions: list all
cards.a: 5-alpha-reductase I and II inhibition; blocks DHT binding to androgen receptors; alpha-1 blockade; 5-lipoxygenase inhibition

cards.q: Saw palmetto effect on DHT in healthy men (1 week)
cards.a: None on 5-reductase activity, DHT or testosterone

cards.q: Saw palmetto and PSA
cards.a: No lowering after 6 months, so no interference with prostate cancer screening

cards.q: Saw palmetto vs tamsulosin in BPH inflammation (3 months)
cards.a: Greater anti-inflammatory effect on infiltrating prostatic cells

cards.q: Saw palmetto monotherapy vs placebo (17 trials)
cards.a: No significant improvement in most urologic symptoms

cards.q: Permixon (hexane extract) 320 mg/day in BPH
cards.a: Improved nocturia and peak flow; IPSS fell 5.73 points (threshold 3.1)

cards.q: Preferred saw palmetto formulation
cards.a: Hexane liposterolic extract (Permixon); ethanolic and CO2 data insufficient

cards.q: Saw palmetto in guidelines
cards.a: AUA 2020 silent; EAU lists hexane extract for men wanting to avoid sexual adverse effects

cards.q: Saw palmetto common adverse effects (1-3%)
cards.a: Abdominal pain, nausea, diarrhoea, fatigue, headache, decreased libido, rhinitis

cards.q: Saw palmetto rare case-report harms
cards.a: Pancreatitis, liver damage, increased bleeding; causality uncertain

cards.q: Claimed sexual side-effect profile of saw palmetto
cards.a: Less sexual dysfunction than tamsulosin or finasteride (claimed)

cards.q: Reported drug-drug interactions with saw palmetto
cards.a: None reported

cards.q: Saw palmetto standardised extract dose
cards.a: 160 mg twice daily

cards.q: Other names for coenzyme Q10
cards.a: Ubiquinone, CoQ, CoQ10

cards.q: Circulating form of coenzyme Q10 after ingestion
cards.a: Ubiquinol (reduced form)

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 serum levels in Parkinson disease
cards.a: Reduced

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 clinical uses studied: list all
cards.a: Hypertension; heart failure; ischaemic heart disease; prevention of statin-induced myopathy

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 blood pressure effect in earlier trials
cards.a: About 11/7 mm Hg fall; probably exaggerated by bias

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 BP benefit more pronounced in
cards.a: Diabetes or dyslipidaemia

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 ejection fraction gain in heart failure
cards.a: About 3.7% with short-term use (2-28 weeks)

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 heart failure outcome (moderate-quality evidence)
cards.a: Fewer HF hospitalisations and deaths; relative reduction 42%

cards.q: Why low CoQ10 is linked to heart failure
cards.a: It marks advanced disease; it does not predict it

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 after myocardial infarction
cards.a: Very small cut in cardiac deaths and reinfarction (absolute reduction 1.5%); low quality

cards.q: Why statins may cause myopathy via CoQ10
cards.a: Statins block HMG-CoA reductase, which is needed for CoQ10 synthesis

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 for statin-induced myopathy (meta-analysis)
cards.a: No benefit on muscle pain or creatine kinase

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 safety at high dose
cards.a: Well tolerated; rarely adverse effects even at 3000 mg/day

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 GI adverse effects
cards.a: Diarrhoea, nausea, heartburn, anorexia (under 1%)

cards.q: Rare coenzyme Q10 adverse effects
cards.a: Maculopapular rash, thrombocytopenia, irritability, dizziness, headache

cards.q: Why coenzyme Q10 reduces warfarin effect
cards.a: Structural similarity to vitamin K; avoid or monitor closely

cards.q: Coenzyme Q10 dose to replace low endogenous levels
cards.a: 30 mg/day

cards.q: Typical cardiac coenzyme Q10 dose
cards.a: 100-600 mg/day in two or three divided doses

cards.q: Normal plasma coenzyme Q10 in healthy adults
cards.a: 0.7-1 mcg/mL (cardiac doses raise it to 2-3 mcg/mL)

cards.q: Endogenous glucosamine role
cards.a: Substrate for glycosaminoglycans and proteoglycans of articular cartilage

cards.q: Commercial source of glucosamine
cards.a: Crabs and other crustaceans

cards.q: Main supplement use of glucosamine
cards.a: Pain and discomfort of knee osteoarthritis

cards.q: Glucosamine salt forms: list all
cards.a: Sulfate; hydrochloride (recent research shows it ineffective)

cards.q: Crystalline glucosamine sulfate: reported benefit
cards.a: Less pain, better function, less joint-space narrowing at 3 years

cards.q: Why the largest glucosamine trial found no benefit
cards.a: It used the hydrochloride form, shown inferior to sulfate

cards.q: Orthopaedic and rheumatic society advice on glucosamine for knee OA
cards.a: Recommend against it (formulation variability, heterogeneous trials)

cards.q: Glucosamine analgesic effect and onset
cards.a: No direct analgesia; benefit may take 1-2 months

cards.q: Glucosamine sulfate common adverse effects
cards.a: Mild diarrhoea, heartburn, abdominal cramps, nausea

cards.q: Glucosamine and shellfish allergy
cards.a: Cross-allergy unlikely if properly manufactured and purified

cards.q: Glucosamine and warfarin
cards.a: Raises INR; bruising and bleeding risk; avoid or monitor closely

cards.q: Oral glucosamine doses used in trials
cards.a: 500 mg three times daily, or 1500 mg once daily

cards.q: Glucosamine benefit in joints other than the knee
cards.a: Unclear

cards.q: Melatonin origin
cards.a: Pineal gland (and other tissues); serotonin derivative made from tryptophan

cards.q: Melatonin secretion pattern
cards.a: Starts about 9 PM, lasts until about 4 AM; suppressed by daylight

cards.q: Strongest zeitgeber for the circadian clock
cards.a: Light

cards.q: Cause of jet lag
cards.a: Mismatch between external time and the internal circadian clock

cards.q: Jet lag symptoms: list all
cards.a: Daytime drowsiness, insomnia, frequent awakenings, GI upset; worst in first 1-2 days

cards.q: Melatonin for jet lag vs placebo
cards.a: Falls asleep faster and sleeps better at destination

cards.q: Best time to take melatonin for jet lag
cards.a: Near target bedtime (10 PM to midnight) on arrival; benefit grows with more time zones

cards.q: Direction of travel where melatonin helps jet lag more
cards.a: Eastbound

cards.q: Non-drug measure for jet lag
cards.a: Daylight exposure on arrival at the new destination

cards.q: Prescription hypnotic developed from melatonin's sleep effects
cards.a: Ramelteon, a melatonin receptor agonist

cards.q: Melatonin in insomnia
cards.a: Improves sleep onset, duration and quality; increases REM sleep

cards.q: Age range where melatonin improved sleep vs placebo
cards.a: 18-80 years

cards.q: Does baseline endogenous melatonin predict benefit of supplement
cards.a: No

cards.q: Melatonin premedication for surgery
cards.a: Reduces preoperative anxiety; may match midazolam

cards.q: Melatonin for postoperative anxiety
cards.a: Mixed results; overall below preoperative anxiety levels

cards.q: Melatonin adjunct in IVF
cards.a: Reduces oxidative stress; may improve oocyte and embryo quality

cards.q: Melatonin teratogenicity in pregnancy
cards.a: None shown; role in preeclampsia under study

cards.q: Melatonin and breastfeeding
cards.a: May decrease prolactin; use cautiously or not at all

cards.q: Melatonin effect on human semen
cards.a: Increases sperm motility; inhibits early apoptosis

cards.q: Common melatonin adverse effects: list all
cards.a: Next-day drowsiness; fatigue; dizziness; headache; irritability

cards.q: Rare melatonin adverse effects
cards.a: Transient depressive symptoms and dysphoria; blood pressure rise or fall

cards.q: Melatonin with antihypertensives: advice
cards.a: Monitor blood pressure, especially when starting

cards.q: Melatonin oral tablet problem and fix
cards.a: Poor dissolution (lack of effect); use chewable or sublingual form

cards.q: Enzyme that metabolises melatonin
cards.a: CYP1A2 (fluvoxamine interacts)

cards.q: Drugs reported to alter melatonin concentrations: list all
cards.a: NSAIDs; antidepressants; beta-adrenoceptor agonists and antagonists; scopolamine; sodium valproate

cards.q: Melatonin and warfarin
cards.a: May shorten prothrombin time; may theoretically reduce warfarin effect; monitor

cards.q: Melatonin and nifedipine
cards.a: Possible rise in BP and heart rate; mechanism unknown

cards.q: Melatonin jet-lag dose
cards.a: 0.5-5 mg; immediate release for 1-3 nights (5 mg acts faster)

cards.q: Melatonin insomnia dose
cards.a: 0.3-10 mg nightly; may repeat after 30 min; maximum 10-20 mg

cards.q: Preferred melatonin formulation for jet lag
cards.a: Immediate release; value of extended release unknown

cards.q: Sustained-release melatonin for insomnia
cards.a: Effective, possibly inferior to immediate release, and costlier

cards.q: Purified supplements of pharmacologic interest: list all
cards.a: Glucosamine; coenzyme Q10; melatonin

cards.q: Ethnopharmacology: definition
cards.a: Scientific study of biologically active traditional agents, which may be beneficial or toxic

cards.q: Pharmacognosy: definition
cards.a: Study of plants or natural sources as possible drugs

cards.q: WHO definition of traditional medicine
cards.a: Knowledge, skills and practices from indigenous cultures for health maintenance and treatment

cards.q: Other names for traditional medicine: list all
cards.a: Alternative medicine; complementary medicine

cards.q: Where and when ethnopharmacology began
cards.a: 16th-century Latin America, by missionaries studying disease-curing plants

cards.q: Claude Bernard's 1857 curare finding
cards.a: Curare blocks motor nerve conduction at the neuromuscular junction

cards.q: Year the term ethnopharmacology was introduced
Founders of molecular ethnopharmacology: list all
cards.a: Luis Lewin; Carl Hartwich; Alexander Tschirch; Richard Evans Schultes

cards.q: Aspirin (1897) and the plant-human link
cards.a: Aspirin came from willow bark; it began the plant-health link

cards.q: Ayurvedic texts and plant coverage
cards.a: Charaka and Sushruta Samhitas describe over 700 plants

cards.q: Rasayana therapy in Ayurveda
cards.a: Natural substances for longevity, memory enhancement and immunomodulation

cards.q: Advantage of traditional knowledge over random screening
cards.a: Raises discovery chances; cuts cost and time

cards.q: Areas where traditional knowledge may help discovery
cards.a: Resistant microorganisms; adverse effects of current drugs; diseases with no known treatment

cards.q: Bioprospecting: definition
cards.a: Systematic search for useful bioresource products for commercial development

cards.q: Main tool for assaying bioprospected libraries
cards.a: High-throughput screening

cards.q: Focus of bioprospecting, given its cost
cards.a: Highly profitable drugs for large global markets

cards.q: Pharmaceutical biopiracy: definition
cards.a: Commercial exploitation of biological or genetic material, often without compensating source people or countries

cards.q: Body mainly responsible for protecting traditional medical knowledge
cards.a: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)

cards.q: Turmeric biopiracy example
cards.a: US patent (1995) for turmeric in wound healing

cards.q: Neem biopiracy examples
cards.a: 1994 hydrophobic neem-oil substance; European Patent Office patent for plant fungal control

cards.q: Hoodia gordonii: patent history
cards.a: Patented 1995 by CSIR; licensed to Phytopharm 1997; Pfizer acquired rights 1998

cards.q: Ayahuasca: source and biopiracy example
cards.a: Banisteriopsis caapi liana bark; 1986 US patent on an ayahuasca variety

cards.q: Physician roles in ethnopharmacology: list all
cards.a: Field work with herbal users; clinical studies of herbs; comparing herbal, modern and combined therapy

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology: direction of discovery
cards.a: Clinics to laboratories (bedside to bench)

cards.q: Conventional drug discovery sequence
cards.a: Molecule, then mice, then man

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology: what comes first
cards.a: Safety, since it starts in humans; efficacy is validated afterwards

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology three pillars: list all
cards.a: Modern science and technology; traditional medicine; modern medicine

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology stages, in order: list all
cards.a: Experiential (record hits); exploratory (develop leads in vitro and in vivo); experimental (safety, efficacy, mechanism)

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology example: aspirin
cards.a: Experiential bleeding observed; experimental work links it to platelet aggregation

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology scope: list all
cards.a: Discover drugs from traditional medicine in use; explain mechanisms; optimise natural leads for safety, efficacy and acceptability

cards.q: Classical drug discovery: alternative name
cards.a: Phenotypic-based (forward) screening

cards.q: Classical approach starting point
cards.a: Functional activity of a hit in cells or animals; target binding later

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology discovery steps, in order: list all
cards.a: Target mining; ligand fishing (binding assay); high-throughput screening; chemical modification; animal functional studies; then clinical studies

cards.q: Target mining
cards.a: Finding molecular targets (protein, enzyme, receptor) using bioinformatics, genomics, proteomics, metabolomics

cards.q: Ligand fishing
cards.a: Binding assays finding compounds that bind the target selectively

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology advantages over classical discovery
cards.a: Cheaper, faster, fewer bottlenecks, higher success rate

cards.q: Ayurvedic reverse pharmacology starting point
cards.a: Clinical experience of traditional healers, or existing databases

cards.q: Golden triangle components: list all
cards.a: Traditional knowledge (Ayurveda); modern medicine; modern science

cards.q: Aim of the golden triangle
cards.a: Newer, safer, cheaper, acceptable and effective therapies sooner

cards.q: Who introduced reverse pharmacology of Ayurvedic drugs in India
cards.a: Sir Ram Nath Chopra and Gananath Sen

cards.q: Sir Ram Nath Chopra
cards.a: Father of Indian Pharmacology; set up first pharmacology research centre in India

cards.q: Rauwolfia serpentina: Sen and Bose (1931) findings
cards.a: Antihypertensive and tranquillising effects

cards.q: Side effects of Rauwolfia noted by Sen and Bose: list all
cards.a: Depression; extrapyramidal syndrome; gynaecomastia; peptic ulcer

cards.q: Guggulipid: source and approval
cards.a: From Commiphora mukul; hypolipidaemic; DCGI approved 1986

cards.q: Bacopa monnieri memory enhancer: developer
cards.a: CDRI, Lucknow

cards.q: Ayurvedic reverse pharmacology lead molecules: list all
cards.a: Picrosides (liver); phyllanthins (antiviral); curcumins (inflammation); guduchi (skin infection); papaya (platelets); rauwolfia alkaloids (hypertension); psoralens (vitiligo); holarrhena alkaloids (amoebiasis); guggulsterones (lipids); mucuna (Parkinson); piperidines (bioavailability); baccosides (memory); withanolides (immunomodulation); ginger (nausea); picrorhiza (hepatitis); curcuma (oral cancer); panchvalkal (burns, wounds); neem (malaria)

cards.q: Old drugs with reverse-pharmacology new indications: list all
cards.a: Thalidomide (multiple myeloma); botulinum (dystonia, blepharospasm); hydroxyurea (fetal haemoglobin induction); aspirin (platelet aggregation); vitamin K2-7 (muscle cramps)

cards.q: Nyctanthes arbor-tristis (night-flowering jasmine): use and result
cards.a: Antimalarial; leaf paste cleared parasites and cured within 7 days

cards.q: CSIR NMITLI herbal drug projects: list all
cards.a: Psoriasis; osteoarthritis; hepatitis; diabetes

cards.q: NMITLI osteoarthritis herbal product
cards.a: Developed with 16 institutes over 5 years; claimed chondroprotective; seeking industry partner

cards.q: Research focus of ICMR reverse pharmacology centre, Mumbai
cards.a: Diabetes, musculoskeletal health, malaria, cancer, neuronal plasticity

cards.q: Indian bodies promoting plant-based drug research: list all
cards.a: Department of Indian System of Medicine; CSIR; NMITLI

cards.q: Reverse pharmacology hurdles: list all
cards.a: Work confined to practitioners or academia; little industry uptake; no structured multidisciplinary organisation; complex purification of curcumins and withanolides

cards.q: Reverse-pharmacology success stories cited as models
cards.a: Artemisinin and reserpine

cards.q: Three main hurdles in drug development that natural leads address
cards.a: Time, money and toxicity

cards.q: Who relies mainly on traditional medicine for primary care
cards.a: The majority of the world's population

cards.q: Major component of traditional medicine
cards.a: Medicinal plants

cards.q: Three basic requisites of any drug
cards.a: Safety, efficacy and quality

cards.q: Plant source of willow-derived analgesics (Table 1.1)
cards.a: Salix alba bark and leaves: salicin, salicylic acid, sodium salicylate; antiplatelet, antipyretic, analgesic

cards.q: Calabar bean (Physostigma venenosum): phytochemical in Table 1.1
cards.a: Eseroline, a reversible cholinesterase inhibitor

cards.q: Ayurvedic plant Withania somnifera (ashwagandha): uses
cards.a: Anti-inflammatory, antistress, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, memory enhancing, antivenom, rejuvenating, antidiuretic

cards.q: Guggul (Commiphora mukul): active class and uses
cards.a: Guggulsterones; hypolipidaemic and anti-obesity

cards.q: Turmeric (Curcuma longa): curcumins used for
cards.a: Inflammation; dietary supplements; cosmetics

cards.q: Mucuna pruriens (Bengal velvet bean): uses
cards.a: Parkinsonism; snake bite

cards.q: Babchi (Psoralea corylifolia): psoralens used for
cards.a: Psoriasis, vitiligo, alopecia

cards.q: Piperidines (black pepper): role
cards.a: Bioavailability enhancers

cards.q: Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri): baccosides used for
cards.a: Memory enhancement

cards.q: Kutaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica): kurchi uses
cards.a: Amoebic dysentery, diarrhoea, IBS, haemorrhoids, liver disorders

cards.q: Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus): uses
cards.a: Reproductive and hormonal problems in women; gastric ulcers, indigestion

cards.q: Amla (Emblica officinalis) fruit: uses
cards.a: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial, CNS stimulant, hypoglycaemic, anticancer, hair growth

cards.q: Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium): uses
cards.a: Anti-reproductive effect; digestive system disorders

cards.q: Papaya (Carica papaya) leaf extract: effects
cards.a: Raises platelet count; antifertility, anti-implantation, abortifacient effects

cards.q: Kutki (Picrorhiza kurroa): picrosides use
cards.a: Hepatoprotection

cards.q: Bhui amla (Phyllanthus amarus): phyllanthins properties
cards.a: Antiviral, immunomodulatory, nephroprotective, anticancer

cards.q: Guduchi (Tinospora cordifolia): lead use
cards.a: Skin infection

cards.q: Withanone (ashwagandha): SARS-CoV-2 target reported in a study
cards.a: Main protease (Mpro)

cards.q: Ashwagandha as a Covid-19 candidate: evidence status
cards.a: A lead only; no clinical outcome data

cards.a: Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals...) Regulations 2016

cards.a: Food, under FSSAI; disease-curing claims fall outside it

cards.a: ICMR recommended daily allowance (RDA); Codex if none

cards.a: "For the dietary management of" the stated condition
